findings.title: Proof-failure cleanup can release a newer unverified epoch
findings.joint: both ownership paths and failure accounting
findings.mechanism: Pre-fetch claim_identity_verified at epoch1 permits an owner-only native release after fetching remote epoch2. Native release reselects highest epoch, so epoch2 receives the release despite the runbook only verifying epoch1.
findings.impact: A different live ownership epoch receives a locally written and committed failed release. Non-fast-forward push refusal does not undo that durable local mutation. No supervisor-admission bypass was observed.
findings.introduced_vs_preexisting: The proof-failure release call is added by this patch. Native owner-only re-selection and the normal post-supervisor release path existed before it; this review does not attribute their entire behavior to the patch.
findings.sufficient_correction: Avoid unqualified cleanup on failed proof and leave reconciliation explicit, or add an expected-epoch comparison at the native mutation boundary with serialization/equivalent protection against claim reselection. A wrapper-only check may race. Native publisher changes need prospective authority amendment.
findings.regression_requirement: Use unchanged/native claim discovery and release in a disposable fixture; fetch reveals newer same-owner epoch; assert no newer-epoch release is written or committed and no supervisor is invoked.
